1 2. Mr. Dale, learned counsel for the appellant would submit that it was a death compensation case filed by the claimants seeking compensation against the death of a pillion rider on a bike.
Mr. Dale would submit that the bike in question was insured by the Insurance Company under Act Only Policy and that the risk of pillion rider was not at all covered by the said policy.

Mr. Dale would submit that despite having raised this defence in the trial, the learned Tribunal even has not discussed this issue in its judgment which is evident from the recitals of the impugned judgment and order.

Mr. Dale would submit that now it is well settled that a pillion rider on a bike or an occupant in a private vehicle which are insured under Act Only Policy/Statutory Policy/Third Party Policy is not covered by such policy, they being not termed as Third Party within the meaning of Chapter-11 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

From perusal of the impugned judgment and award, it reveals that the defence of the Insurance Company, if raised as is argued by Mr. Dale is not at all even touched by the learned Tribunal while adjudicating the claim.

In view of this, issue notice for final disposal, to the respondents, returnable on 12.11.2025.
4.
Call Record and Proceeding.
5. Parties are put to notice that the appeal shall be heard finally at the stage of admission.

6. Mr. Ban h/f. Mr. Gore, learned counsel waives service for respondent nos.1 to 7 including legal representatives of deceased respondent no.6.
7.
The appellant is permitted to serve the respondents by all permissible modes of private service and to file affidavit of service to that effect.
8. The matter be listed after service of notice is complete.
In the meantime, appellant shall take recourse to the provisions enumerated in Chapter II of the Bombay High Court Appellate Side Rules, corresponding to the stage and requirement of matter.
[AJIT B. KADETHANKAR, J.]
